ceilingSources.residentMemoryBytes: rule: 2x the larger measured resident set (62046208 B over the recorded hosts), rounded up to a whole MiB; evidence runtime-budget.evidence/
ceilingSources.idleCpuPercent: rule: 1 percent absolute for an idle crate; measured at most 0.053 percent on the recorded hosts
ceilingSources.wakeupsPerSecond: rule: max(1, 2x the largest 0.3.2 release-iterate whole-process idle rate), rounded up to 0.1/s: ceil(10 * max(1, 2 * max(5.089, 4.859))) / 10 = 10.2/s, from the first 0.3.2 runs (macOS 5.089, Windows 4.859). Unchanged and NOT the synthetic pass/fail gate for this crate since 0.4.0 (ceilingBasis below): it stays the whole-process ceiling for real and installed measurements and for app adoption, so an installed app is still held to a whole-process figure. The whole-process figure moves with host and WindowServer activity (macOS 2026-10-19, back to back: 0.3.3 code 10.78/s after 4.52/s that morning; 0.4.0 10.39/s; bare Wry loop 9.49/s), which is why the crate is gated on the part it owns. macOS measures process interrupt wake-ups; Windows measures live-thread context-switch totals as a proxy. Evidence: runtime-budget.evidence/darwin-arm64-0.3.2-synthetic.txt and win32-x64-0.3.2-synthetic.txt.
ceilingSources.diskOpsPerSecond: design bound: the watchdog threads touch only atomics, the wake bell and the callback (src/watchdog.rs module doc), so the crate issues no disk operations; 1 per second absolute, the sibling crates' floor. Windows measures it (GetProcessIoCounters); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter
ceilingSources.deltaWakeupsPerSecond: rule: 4x the designed watchdog cost, 4 x 1.0/s = 4.0/s. Designed cost: the watchdog's one 1 s main-thread heartbeat (src/watchdog.rs; the other thread never polls). Measured 2026-10-19 on the Mac Mini, back to back at b40195f4: --diagnostic heartbeat-1s 10.488/s minus --diagnostic bare 9.486/s = 1.002/s; full watchdog 10.385/s minus bare = 0.899/s. The gated figure is wake-ups minus a bare Wry loop (no watchdog) measured in the same bench run: bare and watchdog in separate child processes, interleaved bare, watchdog, bare, watchdog, bare, watchdog, and the median pair by delta is reported, so host drift hits both sides. The factor 4 is the same on both hosts: macOS counts about 1 interrupt wake-up per beat, Windows counts per-thread context switches (a proxy) and may see up to 3 per beat (heartbeat thread, main-thread dispatch, return), so 3/s design plus 1/s drift. It passes the designed heartbeat with 3/s of margin and fails a planted extra 100 ms timer (+10/s, delta about 11/s) by more than 2x; any extra timer faster than 250 ms (+4/s) fails, a 1 s timer (+1/s) does not. The absolute whole-process ceiling is not raised.

status.note: The status call returns rightkit_child_process::ProcessUsage (resident and footprint bytes, cumulative CPU seconds, and whole-process wake-up and disk-operation totals where the host reports them: macOS interrupt wake-ups, Windows live-thread context switches as a wake-up proxy, disk operations on Windows and Linux); the rates come from two calls (ProcessUsage::rates_since).

notes: Ceilings come from the recorded measurements by stated rules (ceilingSources); a ceiling left null names its reason below. From 0.4.0 wakeupsPerSecond is gated on a delta (ceilingBasis.wakeupsPerSecond = delta-over-bare): the synthetic bench measures a bare Wry loop and the watchdog back to back and the gate compares watchdog minus bare to deltaCeilings.wakeupsPerSecond, recomputing it from the raw figures; the whole-process figure is recorded as evidence. ceilings.wakeupsPerSecond (10.2, derived from the 0.3.2 whole-process measurements on both hosts) is unchanged and still governs real and installed measurements and app adoption. Measurements for 0.3.2 and 0.3.3 carry no baseline and stay as history; a 0.4.0 synthetic measurement without a baseline is refused, so 0.4.0 needs a fresh run on each required host. diskOpsPerSecond is a design bound (see ceilingSources); macOS exposes no per-process disk-operation counter.
